newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks seen down on Wall St., peso soft.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks seen down on Wall St., peso soft.

text.p: --Mexico stocks seen soft on carry-over, Wall Street
--Peso likely weaker on higher U.S. long bond yield
--Overnight Cetes rate viewed up from low prior close
Dealers saw Mexican stocks opening soft on Thursday on follow-through from Wednesday's declines and an expected decline on Wall Street in the wake of mixed reactions to U.S. economic data.
"There are still profits to take after recent gains, and jitters ahead of the May 20 FOMC meeting," a desk trader said.
Technical analysts situated support for the IPC index at 3,870 points, compared to Wednesday's close of 3,894.20.
Dealers expected the peso to open weaker following mixed reactions to U.S. economic data released early that spurred U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds to recede 16/32 to yield 6.93 percent.
Dealers predicted a trading range of 7.9000/7.9200 per dollar for the benchmark 48-hour peso. Pre-open bids stood at 7.9080/7.9140 per dollar, compared to Wednesday's close of 7.8930/7.8960.
Overnight rates on Cetes were seen opening up from Wednesday's low close of 18.65 percent under pressure from a softer peso and higher U.S. long bond yields.
